newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac calls economic policies a success.
newsitem.headline: Chirac calls economic policies a success.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Wednesday the government's deficit-cutting policies had been a success and pledged to go even further in reducing spending.
"The mastering of public finances means we must go further," government spokesman Alain Lamassoure quoted Chirac as saying, following the centre-right government's weekly cabinet meeting,
Chirac made the comments following an announcement by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis that 1996 public deficits were expected to fall to 4.1 percent of gross domestic product.
"France is beginning to draw the benefits (of its economic policies)," Chirac said. He said the credibility of the government's economic policies had been restored.

The government had set a target of reducing the public deficit to four percent of GDP in 1996 and three percent in 1997, in order to meet the Maastricht criteria for joining the single European currency in 1999.
